chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Jamil from Isma'il al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce of a pregnant woman is one (revocation); so when she gives birth to what is in her womb, she is thereby definitively divorced.

key_terms.وَاحِدَةٌ: One (referring to a single revocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: How many times is a pregnant woman divorced according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir clarifies that a pregnant woman's 'iddah concludes with childbirth, a ruling derived directly from the Quran but elaborated in Shia fiqh to ensure the child's lineage is clear. It underscores the principle that the physical act of delivery serves as the definitive marker for the end of the waiting period, distinguishing it from other forms of 'iddah based on menstrual cycles.
